speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a specific trigger like a puncture wound or insect bite? To help narrow this down, can you describe exactly when the symptoms started and if there is any fluid or pus draining from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That mechanism sounds like a crush or avulsion injury; did you notice any visible skin tearing, exposed bone, or a gap in the finger? Also, have you experienced any numbness or tingling in that finger since the incident?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Tenosynovitis (likely due to the crush injury described, but the absence of the classic "hot potato" signs and the specific history of catching the finger suggests a traumatic tendon sheath injury or early septic tenosynovitis requiring immediate attention). Given the X-ray shows only soft tissue swelling and the history of trauma, I suspect inflammation of the flexor tendon sheath. Have you noticed the finger held in slight flexion with pain on passive extension, or does the finger feel "locked" in place?

REQUEST IMAGES: Please return the ultrasound of the Right Hand to visualize the flexor tendons and sheath.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
